positions.commentary: The speaker notes that Uber is a good example of software affecting the physical world but doesn't fully fit the 'boring' category.
The speaker uses Comcast as an example of a company people assume you have to yell and scream at to negotiate with.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should look for 'boring' technology companies that solve problems with software first rather than adding more people, and that the future of asset allocation includes collectibles like trading cards and video games which will grow explosively.

claims.claim: The speaker expresses admiration for Amazon Web Services, calling them great.
claims.quote: I've always loved Amazon Web Services. I think they're great.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Uber is a good example of software affecting the physical world but doesn't fully fit the 'boring' category.
claims.quote: And I wonder, say how and how not Uber is a good example of this, because it's a consumer application. So it's not necessarily an API, but it's software that affects the physical world.

claims.claim: The speaker uses Comcast as an example of a company people assume you have to yell and scream at to negotiate with.
claims.quote: I remember, like, early on, I'll use Comcast as an example, unfortunately. People always assume that, like, okay, at the end of the month, you have to call Comcast because they overcharged you and you have to negotiate and you have to yell and scream otherwise you're going to get your way.

claims.claim: The speaker is bullish on the industry and views Alt as a trustworthy company solving problems with software first.
claims.quote: I'm very bullish on the industry. You're talking about buying the card in the industry. And so it's basically buying the Apple if you're thinking, if you want to have market exposure to tech.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Alt is a technology company that solves problems with software first rather than adding more people.
claims.quote: Every time we have a problem, we are solving it with software first. So we are a technology company. If we were saying, hey, every time we need to go do something, let's add more people.

claims.claim: The speaker predicts collectibles will become a staple asset class like real estate and precious metals, with explosive growth in trading cards and video games.
claims.quote: I think trading cards in general are all going to experience explosive growth. I think video games, again, the nostalgia factor. Literal video games, like the cartridges and discs.

claims.claim: The speaker defines a good investor as someone who takes the same amount of risk as the S&P 500 and outperforms it, requiring discipline and removing emotion.
claims.quote: If a fund manager took the same amount of risk that the S&P 500 did and outperformed it, that is a good investor. Because for the same unit of risk, they got a higher return on an objective manner.
